extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining whether a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or international application publication is prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), and what filing/benefit/priority dates apply (including provisional/nonprovisional benefits and special rules for international applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support by provisional for benefit/earlier date
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application can provide the critical reference date under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) only if at least one claim of the reference patent, patent application publication, or international application publication is supported by the written description of the relied upon provisional application in compliance with pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, or 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2136.03, subsection III and examples (e.g., examples 2, 4, and 7). Case citations: Amgen Inc. v. Sanofi; Dynamic Drinkware v. National Graphics. The provisional must describe the subject matter relied upon in the reference in compliance with the written description requirement to antedate the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: International application (IA) filed on/after Nov 29, 2000 — three-condition test
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application (IA) was filed on or after November 29, 2000, designated the United States, and was published under PCT Article 21(2) in English, then the international filing date is a U.S. filing date for prior art purposes under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the IA properly claims benefit to an earlier-filed U.S. or IA, apply the reference as of the earlier filing date provided 35 U.S.C. 120/365(c) and 35 U.S.C. 112(a)/pre-AIA 112 support requirements are met. If the IA claims benefit to a provisional, the provisional support rules (see above) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: IA filed on/after Nov 29, 2000 but not designated US or not published in English
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application filed on or after November 29, 2000 that did not designate the United States or was not published in English under PCT Article 21(2) does not have its international filing date treated as a U.S. filing date for pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such references may be applied under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of their publication dates, or under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) only as of a later U.S. filing date of an application that properly claimed the benefit of the IA (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: IA filed prior to Nov 29, 2000 — former 102(e) treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications filed prior to November 29, 2000 are subject to the pre-AIPA (as in force on November 28, 2000) version of 35 U.S.C. 102(e): for U.S. patents, apply as of the earlier of the date of completion of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2),(4) or the filing date of a later-filed U.S. application that claimed the benefit of the IA; application publications resulting from such IAs are not to be applied under 102(e) but under 102(a) or (b) as of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IAs filed before Nov 29, 2000, WIPO publications may still have earlier 102(a)/(b) dates; follow the three subrules in MPEP § 2136.03.B and examples 5–9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit of a nonprovisional U.S. parent under 35 U.S.C. 120
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. patent or patent application publication that claims the benefit of an earlier U.S. nonprovisional application (continuation, divisional, CIP) will be accorded the earlier filing date for pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) purposes only if the earlier-filed application properly supports the subject matter relied upon in the rejection in compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the earlier parent does not support the relied subject matter, the earlier filing date cannot be used to antedate the reference. See MPEP § 2136.04 and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference must itself contain the relied subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: When using a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or international application publication to reject under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), the disclosure relied upon must be present in the issued patent or application publication itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portions canceled in prosecution are not part of the patent/publication and cannot be relied upon (Ex parte Stalego). Subject matter disclosed in an abandoned parent but not carried into the child cannot be used (In re Klesper). Subject matter disclosed in a parent but not included in a CIP cannot be relied on for a rejection over the CIP (In re Lund).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canceled or non-carried subject matter not available
rubrics_metrics.description: Portions of an application that were canceled (or subject matter disclosed in an abandoned parent but not carried over) are not part of the patent or application publication and cannot be relied on in a pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte Stalego; In re Klesper; In re Lund illustrate that canceled examples or material omitted from the issued/published document are not available as part of that reference's disclosure for 102(e) purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire disclosure of patent/publication may be relied on
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), the entire disclosure of a U.S. patent, a U.S. patent application publication, or an international application publication having an earlier effective U.S. filing date can be relied upon to reject the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sun Studs, Inc. v. ATA Equip. Leasing, Inc. (Fed. Cir. 1989) supports that any part of the issued/published disclosure may be used as prior art under 102(e). See MPEP § 2120.01 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: When no common assignee/applicant/inventor — unpublished application remains confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no common assignee, common applicant, or common inventor and the application was not published pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b), the confidentiality under 35 U.S.C. 122(a) must be maintained and no rejection can rely on the earlier-filed, unpublished application (or subject matter not supported in a redacted publication) as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unpublished application must be allowed to issue (if it will not be published) before it can be used as prior art. For copending filings within certain time windows, consider interference procedures per MPEP Chapter 2300 and pre-AIA 102(g) issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common inventor/assignee/applicant permits provisional 102(e) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When at least one common inventor or applicant exists between applications, or the applications are commonly assigned, and the effective filing dates differ, a provisional rejection of the later-filed application over the earlier-filed, unpublished application may be made under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional rejections put applicant on notice early and can be overcome by the same means as a 102(e) rejection, or by abandoning and refiling combined subject matter. Use form paragraph 7.15.01.fti when making such provisional rejections. See In re Irish and Ex parte Bartfeld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection under 103(a) using 102(e) prior art — 103(c) limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) using prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) is not proper if the application contains evidence that the application and the prior art reference were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person at the time the invention was made (pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after Nov 29, 1999 or pending on/after Dec 10, 2004, check for common ownership or obligations under the CREATE Act and MPEP §§ 2146–2146.03. If disqualified under 103(c), do not use the 102(e) reference in a 103(a) rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority date cannot be used as pre-AIA 102(e) date
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign priority dates claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d), (f) or 35 U.S.C. 365(a) cannot be used as pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) reference dates; pre-AIA 102(e) is limited to certain references filed in the United States before the invention by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may attempt to antedate a reference by proving entitlement to the foreign priority date for their own filing (see Hilmer I). See MPEP § 216 for procedures on applicant's right of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of reference is filing date — conception/reduction irrelevant absent 102(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) references, the effective prior art date is the filing date of the reference (which may include certain international filing dates); the date of conception or reduction to practice disclosed in the reference is not relevant to antedating absent issues under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interference is not at issue, do not rely on earlier inventive activity in the reference to antedate it. See Sun Studs v. ATA Equip. Leasing and MPEP §§ 2120.01, 2138.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of parent application subject matter — CIPs and abandoned parents
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter disclosed only in an abandoned parent but not carried into the child, or disclosed in a parent but omitted from a CIP, cannot be relied on in a pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection over the child/published CIP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In re Klesper and In re Lund illustrate that only what is present in the issued/published reference document counts for 102(e) purposes; examine the chain of filings to ensure the relied subject matter was actually included in the reference as filed or published.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(e) references may be used in 103 obviousness rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. patents and certain application/publication references that are available under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) may be used as of their filing dates to show that claimed subject matter is anticipated or obvious (i.e., combined with other prior art in a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hazeltine Research v. Brenner and related precedent permit using earlier-filed patents/publications (as of their filing dates) in 103 rejections. See MPEP § 2146 et seq. for interplay with common ownership/joint research agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection remedies and applicant options
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection may be overcome in the same manner as a full 102(e) rejection; it can also be overcome by abandoning the applications and filing a new application containing the subject matter of both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional rejections give applicant fullest opportunity to overcome by amendment or evidence since copending applications often have the same assignee. Use the designated form paragraph when issuing provisional rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'by another' — difference in inventive entity
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is any difference in the inventive entity between the applicant and the reference, the reference qualifies as being 'by another' for pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess inventive entity accurately; if inventive entities differ, the reference is treated as being 'by another' and is potential prior art under 102(e).
